findings.desc: packages/main/src/tasks/managed-cross-provider-suite-smoke.ts:1 — the 12 test files added by this story (managed-host-run-smoke, managed-host-run-command-smoke, managed-host-run-process-smoke, managed-host-run-e2e-smoke, managed-review-evidence-smoke, proof-admissibility-registry-smoke, provider-process-registry-smoke, provider-execution-inventory-contract, provider-launch-owner-admission-suite, managed-cross-provider-suite-smoke, delivery-check-native-attestation-smoke, native-review-fixture; ~7900 lines) are executed by NO automated regression gate. Verified three independent ways: (1) none appear among the 57 tasks/*.js roots in lattice.config.json validate.commands; (2) none are reachable from the root package.json test:serial-reference consumed by full-suite-runner (npm test / doneRequiredCommands); (3) execution-only transitive reachability from validate roots finds none. lattice.config.json:144-150 registers the aggregate suite ONLY under validate.evidenceCommandTimeoutOverrides, which validation-executor.ts:661-664 consumes solely as a per-command timeout for verification-evidence commands — it schedules no execution. The suite currently PASSES when run manually (I ran it end-to-end), so this is a wiring gap, not broken tests: the adversarial matrices that underpin this story's core safety claims (receipt forgery/staleness/cross-story negative controls, controller non-impersonation, ledger-off slot contention, process-group cleanup, silent-but-live continuation) will not fail CI if a future change regresses them. Severity scoped to medium because the pattern predates this story (host-run-usage-smoke and cross-host-review-smoke are likewise absent from npm test on main), so this amplifies an established repo norm rather than introducing a regression.
